differences.new: PETASOS_RECONFIGURED: live config.yaml change applied to the running session
differences.reason: The plugin's empty-cache log on the first call consumed the 30s attribution window, so re-arming was silent. The enforcer oracle's token is a counter, so re-arming counts as a change and is logged. The Hermes token is the four settings: re-arming restores the same values, the switch is applied, and there is no second configuration change to log.

Hermes v0.23.1 has no profile-change event, and nothing in the host fires one. The old plugin logged this by a handler that was only reached when a test called it directly. The enforcer never emitted it. The Hermes adapter does not either: a relative home is not a settings change on the active profile.
Rejecting a relative profile home was that unreachable handler. Hermes does not deliver the event, so neither adapter logs a skip. The active profile's settings stay as they were.

Hermes v0.23.1 has no profile-change event. The old handler logged the name only when called directly, and it has never run under the host. The step's settings are applied as the active profile's settings. Neither adapter logs a profile-change line.

That resolution line was the unreachable profile-change handler naming a directory the host did not switch to. Hermes reads the active profile's settings at call time. Neither adapter logs a profile path for this step.

Those enabled flags are restart settings. The swapped profile turns the scanners on after they were off. The enforcer reports restart-only changes and does not rebuild scanners, which is the redesign's live-apply rule. The plugin dropped the change silently.
